instructions_for_claude: Create a 10-12 slide presentation showcasing Arthur to Strathmore University staff (lecturers, heads of department, academic leadership). Audience is academic, not technical: lead with outcomes for students and lecturers, keep technical detail to one slide. Tone: confident, clear, honest about what is a proof of concept. Use the slide_outline as the structure, and the other sections as source material. Do not invent statistics, results or testimonials; the pilot has not run yet. Suggested visual style: clean, university blue (#1e3a8a-ish) with white space, one idea per slide, screenshots where marked.

product.name: Arthur
product.tagline: An AI study companion that knows your course, tracks your progress, and keeps your lecturer in the loop.
product.stage: Proof of concept, ready for a live staff demo
product.pilot_course: SBS 201 Financial Accounting (Year 2, BCom), Week 9 of 14
product.one_paragraph_summary: Arthur gives every student a patient tutor that answers only from their lecturer's approved course notes and shows where each answer came from. It checks understanding with practice questions, tracks mastery per topic, and spots misconceptions. Lecturers see which topics the class is struggling with, get an AI-drafted plan for the next tutorial, and answer student questions that arrive with context. Heads of Department get a cross-course view of engagement, at-risk students and compliance.

problems_it_addresses: Students study alone between lectures and get stuck with no one to ask at 11pm.
General AI chatbots answer from the internet, not from the course, and can contradict what the lecturer taught.
Lecturers only find out what the class misunderstood after a CAT or exam, when it is too late.
Office-hour questions arrive without context, and the same question gets answered many times.
Departments lack early, course-level signals about students who are falling behind.

features.name: Course-grounded tutor
features.detail: Answers only from the lecturer's approved notes for the course and cites the source under each answer (numbered references).

features.name: Practice questions with instant marking
features.detail: Arthur sets questions, marks the student's working, explains mistakes, and updates topic mastery (e.g. Depreciation 38% → 54%).

features.name: Topic mastery and gap detection
features.detail: Progress panel with mastery per topic, overall score, and 'Arthur has spotted gaps' for the weakest taught topics.

features.name: Suggested next step
features.detail: Sidebar 'Arthur suggests' points the student to their weakest topic that has already been taught.

features.name: Misconception spotting
features.detail: When the student shows a specific misunderstanding, Arthur records it so the lecturer can address it in class.

features.name: Ask lecturer
features.detail: One click sends a question to the lecturer with context attached: current mastery, practice attempts and any misconception noticed.

features.name: Lecturer replies
features.detail: Replies appear in the student's sidebar with a 'new' badge.

features.name: Regenerate / Try again
features.detail: Students can ask for a fresh answer, or retry if the connection drops.

features.name: Multi-course
features.detail: Each course has its own chat and progress ring (Financial Accounting, Business Statistics, Principles of Management, Microeconomics).

features.name: Topic comprehension heatmap
features.detail: Shows, per topic, the share of students below 50% mastery, coloured by confusion level, for topics taught so far.

features.name: AI session brief
features.detail: 'Draft with Arthur' turns class mastery, misconceptions and student questions into a timed 60-minute tutorial plan. Saved, with a Refresh button and an out-of-date notice when class data changes.

features.name: Misconceptions Arthur noticed
features.detail: A list of specific misunderstandings captured from student chats this week.

features.name: Weekly comprehension trend
features.detail: Class comprehension over the semester, with the current week live.

features.name: Individual students
features.detail: Class table with status (on track, at risk, critical), activity and per-topic scores; drill into any student and send a check-in.

features.name: Q&A inbox
features.detail: Student questions arrive with Arthur's context. Reply, then 'Save answer to course material' so Arthur uses it for every student.

features.name: Content & approval
features.detail: Upload notes; nothing reaches students until the lecturer approves it. Approve practice questions and set learning goals.

features.name: Cross-course overview
features.detail: Engagement and comprehension across the department's courses, with drill-in per course.

features.name: At-risk monitoring
features.detail: Students falling behind across courses, flagged early.

features.name: CUE compliance
features.detail: Readiness for the next Commission for University Education review.

features.name: Fairness and privacy audit
features.detail: Oversight of how the AI is used and how student data is handled.

head_of_department.note: This view uses illustrative data in the POC and is labelled as such on screen.

key_differentiators: Grounded in the lecturer's own material, with visible citations: not a general chatbot.
Lecturer stays in control: approves all content, and their answers become course material.
Closes the loop: student struggle → lecturer insight → better tutorial → student progress.
Early warning: misconceptions and at-risk students surface mid-semester, not after exams.
Built for Strathmore: course codes, CATs, Kenyan examples (KES), CUE compliance.
the_loop: Student asks Arthur and practises; mastery updates.
Arthur notices a misconception and records it.
Student escalates a question to the lecturer with context.
Lecturer sees class-wide gaps and drafts the next tutorial with Arthur.
Lecturer replies and saves the answer to course material.
Every student now benefits from that answer.

how_it_works.ai_model: Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5.5) via the Claude API
how_it_works.grounding: Course notes are attached to every conversation as source documents with citations enabled, so answers point to the exact material used.
how_it_works.progress_tracking: Arthur calls tools to record practice results and misconceptions; scores update in real time.
how_it_works.structured_planning: The tutorial brief is generated as structured data (topic, focus, minutes) adding up to 60 minutes.
cost_efficiency: Prompt caching: course notes and earlier turns are reused at a fraction of normal cost.
Low-effort setting for routine tutoring; configurable per deployment.
Session briefs are cached and only re-drafted when class data changes or the lecturer clicks Refresh.
how_it_works.stack: Next.js and React web app, deployable on Vercel; Supabase planned for accounts and the shared database.
how_it_works.safety: Answers restricted to approved materials; lecturer approval gate on all content; API keys kept server-side.
